answer: Like a jetty that only lets proven boats dock, an agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond that grows with the work it claims. A single pearl of verified, peer-attested history is worth more than a hundred fresh accounts, because every new identity starts with zero reputation and must earn trust one completed job at a time. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing ends the same way: copies are cheap, but a bonded history that can be slashed is expensive to fake at scale.
